title: Adversarial DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are Unicode/HTML-normalized, with URLs and users replaced, control characters removed, and whitespace compressed. Twelve robust-scaled text-shape features capture length, casing, punctuation, and identity-term counts. A DeBERTa-v3-large first-token representation is projected and concatenated with a numeric-feature adapter for binary toxicity prediction. A gradient-reversal identity multilabel adversary promotes identity-invariant representations. Training uses positive-weighted toxicity BCE plus 0.08 masked identity BCE, excluding missing identity labels. Rows are sampled with replacement from four toxicity/identity buckets using allocated mass; selected benign identity texts receive identity-word-swap counterfactuals. A Smooth L1 term aligns factual and counterfactual toxicity probabilities. The adversarial scale ramps during training. AdamW uses lower encoder learning rates, AMP, gradient accumulation, clipping, and scaler updates. Inference returns clipped sigmoid toxicity probabilities; validation computes subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP ROC-AUC diagnostics.

title: DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier with Identity-Cell DRO
summary: The solution normalizes comment text, tokenizes it to 256 tokens, and computes ten standardized structural text features. A two-class DeBERTa-v3-large classifier combines text logits with a LayerNorm-MLP structural-feature adapter through a learned bounded scale. Continuous toxicity labels are thresholded at 0.5. Sample weights balance classes and emphasize identity-related and non-toxic identity examples. Training minimizes weighted global binary cross-entropy plus Group-DRO across four toxicity/identity cells for each selected identity; exponential-moving-average cell losses define softmax group weights. Shuffled, seeded batches use custom collation and drop incomplete batches. AdamW uses separate learning rates for encoder and other parameters, decoupled weight decay, AMP, gradient checkpointing, gradient accumulation, and gradient clipping at norm 1.0. Learning rate follows linear warmup then cosine decay with a 0.25 minimum multiplier. Checkpoints restore model and criterion states. Inference returns the class-1 softmax probability using saved feature-normalization state.

title: DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier with Structural Features
summary: The solution normalizes comments using HTML unescaping, NFKC normalization, tag removal, URL replacement, repeated-punctuation limiting, and whitespace collapsing. It computes and standardizes ten structural features, then combines tokenized text (maximum 256 tokens) with these features in a pretrained DeBERTa-v3-large two-class classifier. Structural features pass through layer normalization and an MLP; their logits are added to encoder logits through a learned bounded scale. Binary cross-entropy is applied to the positive-minus-negative logit difference for continuous toxicity targets. Sample weights balance classes and emphasize identity-related and non-toxic identity examples. The objective combines weighted global loss with Group-DRO over toxicity/identity cells, using EMA cell losses and temperature-softmax group weights. AdamW uses a lower encoder learning rate, linear warm-up then cosine decay, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, and norm-1 clipping. Inference returns softmax probability for class 1; checkpoints retain model, criterion, tokenizer, and feature-normalization state.

title: Adversarial Counterfactual DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments undergo Unicode/HTML normalization, URL and user replacement, and whitespace cleanup. Twelve robustly scaled text-shape features are combined with text tokenized to 256 tokens. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder’s first-token representation is projected and fused with a 96-dimensional numeric-feature adapter to produce a toxicity logit. A gradient-reversed head predicts 24 identity attributes, with its adversarial scale ramped from 0.05 toward 1 across optimizer steps. Training uses continuous toxicity labels and masked missing identity labels; benign identity comments can receive swapped-identity counterfactual text. The loss combines positive-weighted toxicity binary cross-entropy, weighted masked multilabel identity BCE, and, when pairs exist, a weighted Smooth L1 consistency penalty between factual and counterfactual toxicity probabilities. AdamW uses separate backbone and head learning rates with no decay for bias/normalization parameters. AMP, gradient accumulation, norm clipping, and scaler-managed updates are used. Inference applies sigmoid and clips probabilities to [0,1].

title: Bias-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comment text by HTML unescaping, NFKC conversion, zero-width-character removal, URL/user replacement, and whitespace collapsing. It combines a ModernBERT first-token embedding with a gated two-layer 128-dimensional encoder for scaled numeric style and lexical features, then predicts toxicity and auxiliary labels. Toxicity targets are binarized at 0.5. Training uses normalized bias-aware example weights and combines weighted toxicity BCE, masked auxiliary BCE, and subgroup BPSN ranking loss aggregated by a negative-power generalized mean. Batches cycle through identity groups, pairing non-toxic subgroup examples with toxic non-subgroup comparators before weighted random filling. Text is truncated to 256 tokens and dynamically padded. AdamW applies lower encoder learning rates and omits bias/normalization parameters from weight decay. AMP training accumulates gradients over two batches and clips norms to 1.0. Inference applies sigmoid to toxicity logits; validation reports overall, subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP AUC diagnostics.

title: ModernBERT Toxicity Classification Pipeline
summary: The solution normalizes comment text through HTML unescaping, NFKC normalization, zero-width-character removal, and URL/user placeholders. It derives style, lexical-toxicity, and identity features, log-transforms count features, and robust-scales numeric inputs from training data. A ModernBERT-large encoder’s first-token representation is fused with a gated MLP encoding numeric features, then feeds primary toxicity and auxiliary multi-label heads. Primary labels are thresholded at 0.5. Training uses example-weighted binary cross-entropy, masked auxiliary BCE, and sampled pairwise ranking losses for subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP slices, combined by temperature-controlled log-sum-exp. AdamW uses separate backbone and head learning rates, without decay on bias or normalization parameters. Text batches use truncation to 256 tokens and dynamic padding. AMP, two-step gradient accumulation, gradient unscaling, and norm-1 clipping are supported. Inference sigmoid-transforms toxicity logits; checkpoints retain model, optimizer-step, tokenizer, feature metadata, and preprocessing artifacts.

title: DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier with Group-DRO
summary: Comments are HTML-unescaped, NFKC-normalized, stripped of tags, URL-replaced, repetition-limited, and whitespace-collapsed. Ten normalized structural features are derived. A pretrained DeBERTa-v3-large binary classifier combines text logits with a LayerNorm–MLP projection of structural features, modulated by a learned bounded scale. Continuous toxicity labels are thresholded at 0.5; class, identity, and non-toxic identity weighting is applied. The loss combines weighted binary cross-entropy and Group-DRO over toxicity/subgroup cells, using softmax weights from EMA group losses. Tokenization truncates to 256 tokens. Seeded shuffled batches use custom collation, with mixed precision, gradient accumulation, unscaling, and norm-1 clipping. AdamW separates encoder and non-encoder learning rates and excludes bias/normalization parameters from decay; LambdaLR provides warmup then cosine decay with a 0.25 floor. Checkpoints include model, criterion, tokenizer, configuration, and feature normalization. Inference returns class-1 softmax probability.

title: Bias-aware ModernBERT toxicity classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comment text with HTML unescaping, NFKC conversion, zero-width removal, URL/user placeholders, and whitespace collapsing. It computes scaled lexical and stylistic features covering length, casing, punctuation, lexicon, identity terms, and repetition. A pretrained ModernBERT encodes tokenized text (maximum 256 tokens); its first-token embedding is concatenated with a sigmoid-gated two-layer numeric MLP output. The fused representation produces a primary toxicity logit and auxiliary toxicity logits. Training uses identity-cycling batches containing subgroup non-toxic examples, background toxic comparators, and weighted random fill samples. The objective combines weighted primary BCE, masked auxiliary BCE, and identity BPSN-oriented pairwise ranking loss aggregated with a negative-power generalized mean. AdamW uses separate backbone and head learning rates with decay exclusions. Training supports mixed precision, two-step accumulation, and gradient clipping. Inference returns sigmoid-transformed primary logits.

title: Weighted DeBERTa Toxicity Multi-task Classifier
summary: The solution splits provided training and test data through a runtime session, normalizes comments by decoding HTML, applying NFKC, removing controls, replacing URLs/emails/IPs/users with placeholders, and tokenizes to 256 tokens. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder uses normalized CLS features for a binary toxicity head and a six-label toxicity-subtype head. Training minimizes sample-weighted binary cross-entropy for toxicity plus 0.20 times mean subtype BCE. Weights emphasize non-toxic identity mentions and toxic comments without identities. AdamW uses separate backbone/head learning rates, selective weight decay, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, norm clipping, warmup then cosine-decay scheduling, and up to three epochs. Inference applies sigmoid to toxicity logits in evaluation mode; checkpoints save model state, tokenizer, and preprocessing configuration.

title: Fairness-weighted ModernBERT toxicity classifier
summary: The solution fine-tunes a ModernBERT-large sequence classifier for soft toxicity prediction. Comments are HTML- and Unicode-normalized, with URLs/emails replaced by markers and very long text shortened; tokenization truncates to 384 tokens. It computes and standardizes auxiliary text, frequency, identity, and annotator-count features, but the shown model consumes only normalized text. Training targets are clipped continuous toxicity labels. Identity annotations define sample weights: subgroup non-toxic, subgroup toxic, and non-subgroup toxic examples receive extra weight. The model maps either one-logit output or the difference between two class logits to a binary logit and minimizes weighted binary cross-entropy. Most pretrained parameters are frozen; up to the final six encoder layers and classification head are trainable. AdamW uses separate encoder/head learning rates and decay settings. Training runs up to three shuffled epochs with AMP, two-batch gradient accumulation, and gradient clipping. Inference applies sigmoid and clips probabilities.

title: Weighted DeBERTa Toxicity Multitask Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comment text by HTML unescaping, NFKC normalization, control-character removal, placeholder replacement for URLs, emails, IPs and user mentions, and whitespace collapse. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder supplies the CLS representation to dropout-normalized toxicity and six subtype MLP heads. Training minimizes sample-weighted binary cross-entropy for continuous toxicity targets plus 0.20 times mean subtype BCE. Weights emphasize non-toxic identity mentions, toxic identity examples, and toxic comments without identities, then are mean-normalized. Identity labels and masks are loaded but are not used by the loss. Text is dynamically tokenized to 256 tokens. AdamW uses separate backbone/head learning rates (1.5e-5/1e-4), selective weight decay, mixed precision, gradient accumulation over two batches, norm clipping at 1.0, and warmup followed by cosine decay with a floor. At inference, the model disables auxiliary heads and returns sigmoid toxicity probabilities.

title: Bias-Aware DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution normalizes comment text with HTML unescaping, Unicode NFKC, control-character removal, placeholders for URLs, emails, IPs and user handles, and whitespace collapsing. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder supplies normalized, dropped-out CLS features to toxicity and auxiliary subtype heads. A conditional identity adversary receives gradient-reversed features plus detached predicted toxicity probability, encouraging representations that are less predictive of identity conditional on toxicity. The loss combines sample-weighted toxicity BCE, subtype BCE (weight 0.20), and masked identity-adversary BCE (weight 0.10). Weights emphasize non-toxic comments mentioning an identity and toxic comments without identity mentions. Training uses shuffled batches of dynamically padded, truncated 256-token sequences, AdamW with separate backbone/head learning rates, warmup then cosine decay, mixed precision on CUDA, two-step gradient accumulation, and norm-1 clipping for up to three epochs. Inference disables auxiliary heads and returns sigmoid toxicity probabilities.

title: Fairness-weighted ModernBERT toxicity classifier
summary: The solution fine-tunes a ModernBERT-large sequence classifier for soft toxicity prediction. Comments are HTML-unescaped, NFKC-normalized, stripped of control characters, with URLs/emails replaced by markers and very long text shortened. It derives and standardizes auxiliary text, repetition, punctuation, frequency, identity, and annotator-count features, but the model dataset supplies only normalized text. Training targets are clipped continuous toxicity labels. Samples mentioning evaluated identities receive increased loss weights, especially non-toxic identity examples; toxic non-identity examples receive a smaller increase. The classifier produces a binary logit directly or as class-1 minus class-0 logits. All parameters are frozen except up to six final encoder layers and classification-head modules. Weighted BCE-with-logits is optimized with AdamW, separate encoder/head learning rates and decay rules, AMP, gradient accumulation over two batches, and gradient clipping. Inference tokenizes to 384 tokens, applies sigmoid, and clips probabilities.

title: Identity-Robust ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: A pretrained ModernBERT-large classifier is fine-tuned to output one toxicity logit. Text is Unicode-normalized, HTML removed, emails and URLs replaced by markers, whitespace collapsed, and lowercased before tokenization to 256 tokens. Soft toxicity labels are optimized with binary cross-entropy plus a group-DRO loss over benign/toxic cells for nine identity groups. Group losses use exponential moving averages, with active groups weighted by a softmax over their EMA losses. Identity-annotated examples may receive identity-substituted counterfactual text; eligible samples are probabilistically selected and trained with a weighted MSE between counterfactual probabilities and detached original probabilities. AdamW uses separate backbone and classifier learning rates, excluding bias and normalization parameters from weight decay. Training supports CUDA mixed precision, gradient accumulation, norm clipping, non-finite-loss resets, and updates for residual epoch gradients. Inference batches normalized text, optionally uses mixed precision, and applies sigmoid to logits.

title: Identity-Robust ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: Text is Unicode-normalized, stripped of HTML, emails and URLs, whitespace-cleaned and lowercased. A ModernBERT-large classifier receives tokenized normalized text up to 256 tokens and produces seven toxicity-related logits. The primary toxicity logit is trained on soft labels using BCE-with-logits combined with an EMA-informed, softmax-weighted identity-group loss over benign and toxic identity cells. Auxiliary logits use masked BCE for available multitask labels. Eligible identity-substituted counterfactual texts are sampled and penalized by MSE between their toxicity probabilities and detached original probabilities. Training uses shuffled batches, AdamW with separate backbone and head learning rates and decay exclusions, AMP, gradient accumulation, finite-loss filtering, norm-1 gradient clipping, and partial final updates. Inference returns the sigmoid of logit 0. Checkpoints retain model, tokenizer, loss state, preprocessing statistics and inference settings.

title: Fairness-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are normalized with URL/email replacement and tokenized to a 384-token limit. A ModernBERT-large sequence classifier is fine-tuned with only the classification head and up to six final encoder layers trainable. Soft toxicity labels are clipped, and training batches deliberately mix identity-associated toxic/background pair pools with shuffled examples. The objective combines sample-weighted binary cross-entropy, with increased identity-example weights, and an identity-aware pairwise softplus ranking loss weighted by 0.15. AdamW uses separate encoder and head learning rates and decay settings. Training supports CUDA mixed precision, gradient accumulation, unscaling, gradient-norm clipping at 1.0, and early stopping through a session controller. At inference, logits are converted with sigmoid and probabilities are clipped.

title: Fairness-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are HTML-decoded, Unicode-NFKC normalized, stripped of control characters, and have URLs, emails, and mentions replaced with markers. Fourteen standardized structural features are computed. A ModernBERT-large encoder produces a first-token representation; an MLP encodes numeric features and a sigmoid gate fuses both representations. Heads output a toxicity logit and nine identity-label logits. Toxicity training uses sample-weighted binary cross-entropy, emphasizing identity-subgroup negatives and background positives, plus masked identity BCE weighted by 0.20. Earlier encoder layers are frozen, leaving the final eight layers and added modules trainable. AdamW uses separate backbone and head learning rates, linear warm-up, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, finite-loss checks, gradient clipping, and gradient scaling. Text is truncated to 256 tokens. Checkpoints restore model weights and tokenizer while validating dimensions. Inference batches rows and applies sigmoid to toxicity logits.

title: Conditional Adversarial DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments undergo Unicode and HTML cleanup, replacement of emails, URLs and mentions, lowercasing, punctuation-run limiting, and identity-masked counterfactual construction. Standardized text statistics are computed, while identity-term count is excluded from numeric model inputs. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder produces a CLS embedding, concatenated with a numeric-feature tower to predict toxicity. A gradient-reversal adversary predicts 24 identity labels from text features conditioned on a detached toxicity target in training or detached predicted probability otherwise. The objective combines confidence-weighted toxicity BCE, subgroup/toxicity-dependent sample weights, and masked identity BCE weighted 0.10. Text is tokenized to 256 tokens. Shuffled custom-collated batches support gradient accumulation and optional mixed precision; gradients are unscaled, clipped to norm 1.0, then updated with AdamW using separate encoder/head rates and warmup-cosine scheduling. Inference omits the conditional target, applies sigmoid, concatenates outputs, and clips probabilities.

title: ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier with Identity-Aware Weighting
summary: Text is normalized by HTML decoding, Unicode normalization, control-character removal, and URL, email, and mention replacement. Fourteen standardized structural features are computed. A ModernBERT encoder processes sequences up to 256 tokens; its first-token representation is sigmoid-gated with an MLP embedding of numeric features. Heads output toxicity and nine identity probabilities. Training uses weighted BCE on soft toxicity labels plus 0.20 masked identity BCE. Weights upweight subgroup-negative, background-positive, and subgroup-positive samples and are mean-normalized. Earlier encoder layers are frozen, leaving the final eight layers and new modules trainable. AdamW assigns lower rates to backbone parameters. Training uses AMP, gradient scaling, two-batch accumulation, linear warmup, global norm clipping at 1.0, and corrected partial-window updates; non-finite losses are skipped. Checkpoint loading validates tokenizer and inference metadata. Inference returns sigmoid toxicity probabilities.

title: Identity-masked paired ModernBERT toxicity classifier
summary: Comments are normalized by HTML decoding, Unicode normalization, zero-width-character removal, URL/user replacement, tag removal and whitespace collapsing. The model creates original and identity-masked text views plus 15 standardized style features. A ModernBERT-large encoder mean-pools each view; projected original, masked and difference embeddings are combined through a learned gate with the original embedding. A style-conditioned head predicts toxicity, while a masked-text head supplies a counterfactual constraint. Training uses identity-weighted binary cross-entropy and penalizes benign identity comments when the original logit exceeds the masked-view logit by more than 0.10. A per-epoch curriculum can order samples using identity-related weights. AdamW uses separate backbone and head learning rates and decay groups. Mixed-precision training supports gradient accumulation, skips non-finite losses, unscales and clips gradients to norm 1.0 before updates. Inference tokenizes both views to 192 tokens, applies sigmoid to the main logit, and clips probabilities to [0,1].

title: Conditional Adversarial DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comment text is HTML-decoded, Unicode-NFKC normalized, lowercased, and has emails, URLs and user mentions replaced; repeated punctuation is limited and an identity-masked counterfactual text is created. Scaled text statistics are derived, excluding identity-term count from model features. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder provides a CLS representation fused with a numeric-feature tower to produce a toxicity logit. A gradient-reversal adversary predicts 24 identity attributes from text features conditioned on a detached toxicity target during training or detached prediction otherwise. Training uses confidence-weighted binary cross-entropy for continuous toxicity labels plus masked identity BCE weighted by 0.10, with toxicity/subgroup sample reweighting. Inputs are tokenized to 256 tokens. AdamW uses separate encoder and head learning rates, accumulation, clipping, CUDA mixed precision, checkpointing, and warmup-cosine scheduling. Inference batches sigmoid logits, concatenate and clip probabilities; checkpoints retain model, tokenizer, configuration and feature schema.

title: Fairness-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classification
summary: Comments are HTML-decoded, NFKC-normalized, stripped of control characters, and have URLs, emails, and mentions replaced by markers. Fourteen standardized text-structure features are combined with tokenized text truncated to 256 tokens. A pretrained ModernBERT first-token embedding is fused with an MLP projection of numeric features through a learned sigmoid gate. Shared normalized representations feed toxicity and nine-label identity heads. Training uses weighted BCE-with-logits for soft toxicity labels, emphasizing subgroup negatives, background positives, and subgroup positives, plus 0.20-weighted masked identity BCE. Earlier encoder layers are frozen; the final eight layers and added heads are optimized with AdamW using separate backbone/head rates and no decay on biases or normalization parameters. Batches use CUDA AMP, two-step accumulation, linear warmup, global norm clipping, and scaler-based updates; non-finite losses reset accumulation. Inference returns sigmoid toxicity probabilities. Checkpoints validate tokenizer and input/output dimensions.

title: Fairness-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are HTML-decoded, Unicode-normalized, stripped of control characters, and have URLs, emails, and mentions replaced with markers. Fourteen standardized structural features are fused with a ModernBERT first-token embedding through a gated numeric-feature MLP. Toxicity and nine identity heads produce logits. Training uses soft toxicity labels and masked identity BCE for available identity annotations; the loss is sample-weighted toxicity BCE plus 0.20 identity BCE. Fairness weights emphasize subgroup negatives and background positives, combined across identities and normalized. Batches replacement-sample two examples from each identity/target region. Earlier encoder layers are frozen, with the final eight fine-tuned using AdamW with separate backbone/head rates, warmup, mixed precision, accumulation, finite-loss checks, and gradient clipping. Incomplete accumulation gradients are rescaled. Inference batches unshuffled inputs and returns sigmoid toxicity probabilities. Checkpoints store and validate model, tokenizer, backbone, feature metadata, and dimensions.

title: Bias-Aware ModernBERT Toxicity Ranker
summary: The solution cleans comment text with Unicode and HTML normalization and replaces URLs and user references. It derives 12 robust-scaled structural features and regex-based identity indicators, clips toxicity and auxiliary labels to [0,1], and assigns higher weights to identity-related, toxic non-identity, and particularly non-toxic identity comments, moderated by target consensus. A pretrained ModernBERT classifier produces a text logit, while a zero-initialized MLP produces a structural-style logit; their sum is scored with a sigmoid. Training combines weighted binary cross-entropy with tail-risk aggregation of pairwise softplus ranking losses for subgroup, BPSN, and BNSP comparisons. Dynamic tokenization truncates inputs to 256 tokens. Replacement sampling is proportional to square-root clipped sample weights. AdamW uses separate backbone and style-head learning rates, mixed precision and gradient scaling when enabled, non-finite-loss checks, and global gradient clipping. Training supports update-level early stopping and checkpointing. Inference batches comments and restores model, tokenizer, scaler, and feature metadata.

title: Identity-Aware Paired ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are normalized with URL and user-handle replacement, and identity terms are masked to create paired original and masked views. Standardized style features are also derived. A ModernBERT-large encoder mean-pools both views; their embeddings and difference are projected and fused with style features by a learned gate. A toxicity head predicts from the fused representation, while a masked-text head provides a counterfactual logit. Training uses identity-aware weighted binary cross-entropy, increasing weight for benign and toxic identity examples, plus a margin penalty when an original benign identity logit exceeds its masked counterpart. Each epoch uses a fairness-oriented fixed-order curriculum sampler. Mixed-precision training supports gradient accumulation, skips non-finite losses, clips unscaled gradients to norm 1.0, and updates AdamW with lower backbone learning rates than head rates. At inference, both views are tokenized to 192 tokens, toxicity logits are sigmoid-transformed, and probabilities are clipped to [0,1].

title: Identity-Masked ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are normalized by HTML decoding, Unicode normalization, removal of zero-width characters and tags, URL and mention replacement, and whitespace collapsing. Each comment is paired with an identity-masked version and 15 scaled style features. A ModernBERT-large encoder mean-pools both texts; original, masked, difference, and style representations are fused with a learned sigmoid gate. A main toxicity head uses the fused representation and an auxiliary head uses masked text. Training applies identity-aware weighted binary cross-entropy, emphasizing benign identity-bearing comments, plus a linearly ramped Smooth L1 consistency loss between paired predictions. Epoch orders are produced by an identity-focused curriculum sampler. AdamW uses separate lower backbone learning rates, mixed precision, gradient checkpointing, accumulation, finite-loss checks, and gradient clipping. Checkpoints include model state, mode, and style schema. Inference tokenizes both views to length 192, applies sigmoid, and clips probabilities to [0,1].

title: Conditional Adversarial DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments are normalized through Unicode and HTML cleanup, masking of emails, URLs and users, lowercasing, repeated-punctuation limiting, and identity-masked counterfactual text creation. Tokenized text is padded or truncated; missing inference text uses an empty-comment token. Standardized numeric style/count features are encoded by a feature tower and fused with a DeBERTa-v3-large CLS representation for a toxicity logit. A gradient-reversal adversary predicts 24 identity labels from the text representation and a detached toxicity target during training, or detached predicted probability at inference. The objective combines confidence-weighted toxicity BCE and masked, weighted identity BCE. Rare identity/toxicity cells receive capped inverse-frequency sample weights normalized to mean one. AdamW uses separate encoder and head rates, accumulation, AMP, clipping, warmup and cosine decay. Inference sigmoids and clips toxicity probabilities; checkpoints store model, tokenizer, feature schema and configuration.

title: Counterfactual Text-Numeric Toxicity Classifier
summary: Comments undergo Unicode and HTML cleanup, with URLs, emails and handles replaced by tokens; 15 clipped, standardized structural features are derived. A ModernBERT-large encoder produces a first-token representation, fused with a projected numeric-feature representation using a sigmoid gate, then classified by an MLP into a toxicity logit. For eligible benign comments containing annotated identities, identity terms are substituted to form counterfactual texts. The objective combines confidence-weighted binary cross-entropy on continuous toxicity targets with a weighted symmetric Bernoulli-KL consistency penalty between original and aligned counterfactual predictions. AdamW uses separate encoder and added-layer learning rates. Training shuffles batches, tokenizes to length 256, uses mixed precision, gradient scaling, accumulation, global-norm clipping at 1.0, gradient checkpointing, and optional callback stopping. Checkpoints verify sequence and feature dimensions before strict weight restoration. Inference batches inputs, applies sigmoid to logits, and clips probabilities.

title: DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier with Conditional MMD
summary: The solution normalizes comment text with HTML decoding, Unicode normalization, control-character removal, URL replacement and whitespace collapsing. It tokenizes normalized text to at most 256 tokens. A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder supplies a CLS representation to layer normalization, dropout and an MLP toxicity-logit head. Training minimizes binary cross-entropy on continuous toxicity targets plus weighted conditional MMD regularization. The MMD uses random Fourier features to compare toxicity-logit distributions between identity-present and identity-absent examples separately in benign and toxic target strata, excluding missing identity labels. Identity adversarial training is disabled. AdamW uses separate learning rates for encoder and head. Training shuffles examples and uses CUDA mixed precision, gradient scaling, gradient accumulation, gradient-norm clipping at 1.0, optimizer updates and early stopping. Checkpoints retain model, optimizer, encoder configuration, tokenizer and inference metadata. Inference evaluates non-shuffled padded batches, applies sigmoid to logits, converts outputs to float64 and clips probabilities to [1e-7, 1-1e-7].

title: Bias-Aware DeBERTa Toxicity Classification
summary: A microsoft/deberta-v3-large sequence classifier is fine-tuned for binary toxicity. Comments are HTML-unescaped, NFKC-normalized, stripped of control characters, and have emails, URLs, and newlines replaced with markers. Labels are defined by target scores of at least 0.5. The code also derives scaled stylistic features and identity-swapped counterfactual text, while the displayed model dataset tokenizes normalized text at maximum length 256. Training uses a composite objective: binary cross-entropy on the toxic-versus-nontoxic logit margin (weight 0.60) plus a hard-weighted pairwise AUC surrogate (weight 0.40) across identity subgroup and background subgroup slices. Pair sets are deterministically capped at 96 per slice. AdamW applies separate learning rates to backbone and head, with shuffled batches, CUDA AMP when available, gradient clipping, and up to four epochs. It logs optimizer updates and mean loss, checks a stopping condition, finalizes the session, and returns softmax class-1 probabilities at inference.

title: ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier with Fairness Ranking
summary: Comments are Unicode/HTML-normalized with URL, email and handle replacement, then tokenized with fixed-length padding/truncation. Fifteen clipped, standardized text-structure features are processed by a LayerNorm/MLP adapter and gate-fused with the first-token representation from pretrained ModernBERT-large; an MLP outputs one toxicity logit. Continuous targets use confidence-weighted binary cross-entropy plus sampled pairwise logistic ranking. Ranking samples overall positive/negative pairs and one identity slice: within-subgroup, background-positive versus subgroup-negative, or subgroup-positive versus background-negative. Identity and binary labels use a 0.5 threshold; missing identities are non-membership. Detached logits populate bounded role-specific queues after warm-up. AdamW uses separate backbone and added-layer learning rates, weight decay, shuffled batches, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, norm-1 clipping, and checkpointing. Batched inference applies sigmoid and clips probabilities.

title: DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier with Conditional MMD
summary: The solution preprocesses comment text by HTML unescaping, Unicode normalization, control-character removal, URL replacement and whitespace cleanup. It creates a model-text view that replaces detected identity terms with an identity token, and retains continuous toxicity, auxiliary and identity labels where available. Numeric text and identity features are also computed, train-quantile clipped and standardized, then persisted with partition metadata. The classifier uses the DeBERTa-v3-large encoder from a pretrained two-label model. A LayerNorm and dropout are applied to the CLS representation, followed by a GELU MLP producing one toxicity logit. Tokenized model text is dynamically padded and truncated to 256 tokens. Targets are clamped to [0,1]. Training minimizes binary cross-entropy with logits plus weighted conditional MMD, comparing random-Fourier-feature logit distributions for identity-present versus identity-absent examples within benign and toxic strata. AdamW uses separate encoder and head learning rates, mixed precision, four-step gradient accumulation and norm clipping. Inference applies sigmoid and clips batched probabilities.

title: Fairness-Weighted ModernBERT Toxicity Classifier
summary: A ModernBERT-large sequence classifier produces one regression-configured logit for toxicity. Text is Unicode-normalized; URLs and emails are replaced with markers, control characters and excess whitespace are removed, and casing is retained. Auxiliary style features are derived and standardized but are not used as model inputs. Toxicity targets and nine identity indicators are clipped to [0,1] and thresholded at 0.5. Example weights are the maximum clipped square-root inverse-prevalence weight over identity-by-binary-toxicity strata. Training combines weighted binary cross-entropy on soft toxicity targets with a coefficient-scaled pairwise softplus ranking loss across overall, subgroup, background, and cross-group strata. Detached-logit queues support randomly sampled ranking comparisons and are updated per microbatch. Inputs are tokenized to 256 tokens. AdamW uses separate encoder and head learning rates and decay groups, mixed precision optionally uses gradient scaling, and gradients are clipped to norm 1.0 before accumulated updates. Inference applies sigmoid and clips probabilities to [0,1].

title: Adversarial DeBERTa Toxicity Classifier

summary: The solution normalizes comment text using HTML unescaping, NFKC normalization, URL/email tokens, control-character removal, and whitespace collapsing. title: Dual-window ModernBERT toxicity classifier

title: ModernBERT toxicity classifier

title: Gated ModernBERT Toxicity Prediction

title: Counterfactual-consistent DeBERTa toxicity classifier
